thread:
maria: Quick question — ops wants a proxy-level reroute for v1->v2 when v2 has transient errors. Thinking about sticky routing + a tiny sampling rate to collect telemetry. Is this feasible without breaking quotas or billing?

jason: We can do header-based sniffing, then reroute in edge proxy. But need to decide how customer identities map for quota accounting.

lee: If we reroute at the proxy, we should keep a trace header so console and billing see the original target. e.g. `X-Redwood-Orig-Version: v2` then `X-Redwood-Reroute: v1`. That preserves attribution.

amanda: Attribution is the hard part — if we secretly send tokens to v1, which model/price bucket do we charge? ops expect precise deltas for invoices.

sara: Telemetry-wise we want a signal that counts reroutes separately: `reroute.count`, `reroute.latency_delta`, `reroute.success_gain`. Also sample the original prompt for evals (privacy aware).

maria: Agreed. My initial thought: allow reroute only for retries (not first try), and only when v2 returns 5xx or malformed. Keep a config that caps reroute per-customer per-minute.

jason: +1. Also suggest a micro-canary: 0.1% global sampling where we force reroute even on success to measure quality regression. Call it a "silent-sampler" so it doesn't affect production path.

lee: UI question — should console show a banner when reroutes exceed threshold? We could add a badge on model route: "Reroute rate: 0.6% (last 1h)" and a link to traces.

amanda: If we expose reroute rate in console, customer support will see it and escalate. We need a per-customer opt-out toggle for reroute.

sara: For evals, keep sampling pseudonymized. We must ensure PII removal rules still apply when sending samples to v1 for rerun.

jason: Proposed config sketch (edge proxy):
```yaml
reroute_policy:
  trigger_statuses: [502, 503, 504, 422]
  max_per_minute_per_customer: 10
  retry_only: true
  silent_sampler_pct: 0.1
  headers:
    add: {"X-Redwood-Reroute": "v1", "X-Redwood-Orig-Version": "v2"}
```

maria: Nice. Two more things: 1) telemetry flag so metrics immediately show in observability (not delayed); 2) a clear billing decision — charge against the version the customer asked for unless they explicitly pin to v1.

amanda: Billing call: charge to requested version for now, but log the delta as a separate line item for capacity tracking. We'll revisit if customers object.

lee: Rollout UX: offer a console toggle per route: [Enable auto-reroute on errors] with a small explainer and expected cost/latency impact. Also allow a test button to simulate a reroute for a given request ID.

sara: We'll add a telemetry tag `reroute.simulated` for those test button hits so they don't contaminate SLIs.

ops-bot: incident: region-us-west v2 spike 2124999900 -> 2124999955, auto-reroute triggered for 0.4% requests.

deploy-bot: deploy: reroute-proxy-v1.1 -> canary-50% edge on staging at 2125000060 by jason.

maria: Action items: jason to wire proxy implementation + headers, lee to mock console toggle and badge, amanda to draft billing note, sara to add telemetry metrics and PII checklist. Aim for staging canary next Tue.

jason: I can ship a minimal impl that does header-only reroute + metrics. Will include the silent-sampler flag.

lee: I'll prototype the console banner and a per-route toggle. UX copy: "When enabled, requests that fail on the selected version may be routed to a compatible fallback to reduce errors. Reroutes are rate-limited and visible in usage."

amanda: I'll open a billing RFC and include example invoice rows.

sara: I'll add the metrics to the monitoring dashboard and create an alert if reroute_rate > 1% for 15m.

maria: Thanks all — important we ship conservative defaults. We can widen after data. :thumbsup:
